steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook elbow macaroni in the boiling water, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, about 8 minutes; drain well.

Melt 1/4 cup butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Stir in flour and salt; cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes. Whisk in milk and simmer, stirring frequently, until mixture thickens slightly, about 5 minutes.
Turn off the heat and stir in Cheddar cheese, in batches, until cheese is melted. Add macaroni and stir to coat.
Pour into a 9x13-inch baking dish. Mix the remaining 1/4 cup of melted butter and crushed crackers together in a bowl; scatter evenly over macaroni mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown on top, about 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Homemade Macaroni and Cheese
raw_recipe.description: This creamy macaroni and cheese is loaded with Cheddar and baked with a buttery cracker crumb topping for a comforting family favorite everyone loves.

video.description: A buttery cracker topping and rich cheese sauce make it a family favorite.

review.reviewBody: This was really good! I added about a half teaspoon each of paprika and dry mustard, and mixed more grated cheese into the ritz crumbles. Yum!

ok me and my fiance loooove macaroni and cheese. we have tried tons of macaroni and cheese recipes.. but this by farrrrr was our favorite! DELICIOUS! well it also helps that extra sharp cheddar is our favorite cheese and we always have a brick of it in our fridge. EXCELLENT! nice and creamy and the topping was amazing! i used the other reviewers advice and added parmesian to the topping and i also used garlic croutons instead of ritz crackers. THE BEST!

I don't normally try a recipe off this site unless it gets at least 4 1/2 stars from 100 people or more, but I was looking for a recipe that called for simple ingredients that I already had, and this one fit the bill. So I gave it a try, and it was really very good. The only change I made was that I didn't add the cracker crumb topping. I sprinkled extra cheese on top before baking. Everyone in my family loved it, and it was even better the next day! * I will add that the butter/flour/milk/cheese mixture never did thicken on top of the stove, but it firmed up nicely while baking.

I made this for a party. So I doubled the ingredients as listed except for the milk. I followed a posters advice and used 3 cups of milk which I then doubled. Next time I may decrease by 1/2 cup, I used a 6 quart stock pot to make the cheese mixture. I used a 10 x 14 roasting dish to bake. I need to bake for a little bit longer, 30 minutes at 350° I stirred the mixture up, put it in for another 20 minutes, then added the cracker topping and finished off for an additional 15 minutes.

This recipe came out great! Used Cabot bacon cheddar cheese, very nice taste! Baked it a little less time, about 37 minutes.

Really an easy & yummy Macaroni and cheese, and you can pick different cheeses & add ins.

I mixed a ton of reviews together and the flavor was great. Elbow macaroni - 16 oz bag. Don't listen to reviews that say to use less milk; I did and it was too dry. Macaroni soaks it right in. Added ingredients that made the taste great; paprika, pepper, dry mustard, nutmeg and garlic powder. Shredded cheeses added: 1/2 cup parmesan, 1/2 cup gruyère and a little over one cup sharp cheddar. Used buttery crackers but mixed in shredded parm. Completely cooked in 35 minutes. Will make again but will use more milk and most likely will try heavy cream instead.

Simple enough recipe and turns out well. Made a few tweaks: sauted 2.5, medium-sized minced Walla Walla Sweet onions with the butter when I started making the cheese sauce; added 1 Tbs of paprika to the flour and sifted both when added to the sauted onions; when mixing the noodles and cheese sauce added 3 cups of 1/2 -inch cubes of leftover ham we had in the freeze; and topped the crushed Ritz crackers with grated parmesan cheese.

It was ok. I had wayyyyy too much cheese sauce. Thankfully I added it to the pasta a little at a time and only used half of it. The milk and roux never thickened when it simmered, but the cheese did make it thicker. I knew it would set more while it baked, so the consistency ended up being ok. It would have been soup if I’d used all the sauce. The cheese sauce also had a somewhat grainy texture even though my roux was smooth and I used a block of cheddar that I shredded myself. I used sharp cheddar and then added some Parmesan and Monterey Jack that I had on hand because it tasted bland when I sampled it. I would make this again but use half the milk, add different cheeses for a stronger flavor, and add some mustard powder and pepper.

Made for 3 servings with a sharp cheddar and added a small grilled and chopped ham steak. Cut back on the crackers significantly and omitted the extra butter in a 6x9 casserole, served with a small salad. Was 4 servings for 2 adult light eaters. Will try again with dry mustard with ham and a splash of Tabasco. Sour cream and chives would work well if serving as a side dish without meat.

I like this recipe, but it needs a lot more seasoning. I put a little bit of paprika and pepper before it was went into the oven, but it needs more. I also used sharp cheddar. Make sure when you add the milk you do it slowly so you have time to really mix it in with the mixture. Keep whisking. It will eventually thicken up nicely. For the topping I used ground of croutons insteads and just a few crackers and that part is amazing. 45 minutes was the perfect amount of time. It was nice and browned on top, but any longer and the edges would have been burnt. I think this would also be good if you put the cracker crust along the bottom of the pan - honestly that's the best part.

I combined a lot of advice from previous comments and the whole things turned out great!! I added More Spice (instead of paprika because I didn’t have it), onion powder and chopped garlic to the milk/flour/butter mixture before adding in the cheese. I also added an extra handful of the shredded cheese to make it a bit thicker. Definitely want to stir to a roux for best consistency (unless you really want it a bit runnier). I substituted the cheddar for one bag of sharp cheddar and one bag of the Mac and cheese blend cheese. For the topping I substituted Panko bread crumbs (seasoned) and crumbled Parmesan cheese. I still pour led the 1/4 cup melted butter on top. Overall it turned out really well and was a big hit.
no changes was fantastic

My shredded cheese didn’t melt completely. I use pre-shredded cheese from the store and then when I searched it up online, I read that I should shred my own cheese. Otherwise the store bought shredded cheese won’t melt properly. It may help to add that to the instructions, Hoping it will still turn out OK

This was tasty. I cut this in half to make 3 servings, but it still made 5-6. I did use this as a side dish and not a main. This came together fairly quickly. I used a medium cheddar in this. This was cheesy but it seemed too one-sided with just cheddar, and I feel like using a blend of different cheeses would give this more depth. I'd make one of them American as it has a creamy melt, whereas cheddar has a grainy melt. The top with the crunchy crackers was my favorite part along with the toasted corners. Give me an edge serving any time. It did soak up all the sauce and turned out a bit dry, so I'd increase the sauce if I fixed this again. I missed that it didn't have that toasted cheesy layer on top like the cafeterias do, but I did like the crackers. I guess you can't have both.
I ADDED CHOPED CHICKEN FOR EXTRA PROTEIN I USED CRUSHED GARLIC CORUTONS BC IT'S WHAT I HAD ON HAND !!
Ritz crumbles are great ! I’ve always used bread crumbs and Parmesan cheese instead.
I made this as the recipe says and with a little catch up on the sauce part, mine wasn’t heating fast enough, it turned out great and was a big hit at dinner!
The 45 minute cooking time, in my opinion, is too long. It became too dry as a result. Perhaps using a 2 quart deeper casserole dish would help too. Really liked the bread crumb topping.
The best!!! I keep coming back to this recipe time and time again 😊

I've made this a few times now. Once as directed, once with extra salt and pepper, and as others have recommended, yellow mustard. I'm commenting to reassure people who may be trying this for the first time. Cook the pasta under (as the recipe instructs). When you pour everything into the pan, it will be soupy. You may feel like you made a mistake. You didn't, the pasta will absorb the liquid. I just cooked it again tonight and even at 35 minutes in the oven I didn't think it would thicken. It did. It always does. Delicious. Anthony Bourdain always added a glug of Worcester sauce to his Mac and cheese, it adds a umami depth of flavor. Enjoy.
